original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Audit the head-travel, product-count and rounding claims of #4100 PROOF.md's cached chirp prefix-product odometer with a written amortization and a literal four-tape head-movement count.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one quantified implication at its caller; this is the fixed-tape cost implication of the chirp section, whose failure (a per-record d factor) the #4100 ledger itself rejects.
bottleneck_link: A leftover per-record d factor in the chirp would cost power epsilon > 1-kappa and invalidate #4100's proposed exponent; the claimed power-0 phase row depends on this tariff.
stop_rule: Stop once the stated amortized head travel, product count and rounding bound are proved with constants and checked on literal head counts with failing controls.
evidence: README written amortization; verify.py: 36 literal four-tape cases (d up to 12, radices 2..8, factor-two premise) within the per-case bounds and the uniform constant 31 (max 6.997 TP), cache <= 12 TP, counter <= 4T, exact product counts (< 2 per record); 4,820 rounding records at <= 0.754 of (2d-1) sqrt2 2^-P; controls: per-record d scan grows linearly (66 TP at d=12), skewed radices (2,512) reach 258.5 TP, nearest rounding leaves the unit disk (112 entries), ratio updates drift 965x the bound.
author: Ryanson Jonathan, with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance in reading, the amortization proof, simulator implementation and writing; no independent human or proof-kernel review.

open_questions.question: Interleave the chirp stream with the actual polynomial-record payload layout.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The chirp must be emitted in the payload's physical order (axis 0 packed into r-coefficient records) without an extra pass.
open_questions.first_step: Add a packed-record payload tape to the four-tape model and count one pointwise pass.

open_questions.question: Price chirp table setup at the real precision.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the remaining o(V) claim of the section.
open_questions.first_step: Bound elementary cos/sin evaluation at Cp+o(p) bits times d*t entries.
